analysis:
Examined both coding revisions, DaemonStateFile metadata, its complete patch, and supplied surrounding BASE source. The change adds optional AddonHoldSnapshot state (DaemonStateFile.swift HEAD 105–107, 353–356) and symmetric optional decoding/encoding (DaemonState+Coding.swift HEAD 56, 93). Absent fields remain compatible; schema, process identity, lifecycle, trust and App Attest serialization are unchanged. No concrete security regression is established by these additions alone.
The new snapshot reaches the existing diagnostic JSON persistence path (DaemonStateFile.swift BASE 606–624), whose atomic write and schema-checked read are not changed. Relevant integration concerns are operator-visible data under TB-003/A-001, availability and model residency under TB-007/T-029, diagnostic versus serving authority under TB-011/T-052/T-053, and preserving T-041 cache isolation. No changes to encryption, cache scope, attestation admission, billing or privileged helper authority are visible here.
Integration must inspect AddonHoldSnapshot's fields and producers to establish whether serialization exposes request-derived data, credentials or control capabilities, and inspect add-on consumers to verify freshness/process binding and that diagnostic state is not treated as authorization. Those implementations and the add-on socket controls are outside the supplied scope; their absence is not evidence of a missing control. These unresolved contracts prevent a security conclusion about the combined add-on behavior.
